description: The line plot illustrates the performance of different methods for multivariate anomaly detection as measured by the Area Under the Curve (AUC) in percent, plotted against the parameter N, which likely represents the number of neighbors or a similar model hyperparameter. The x-axis, labeled “N,” ranges from 0 to approximately 20 with tick marks at intervals of 5, and the y-axis, labeled “AUC (%)”, spans from 75% to 100% with tick marks every 5 percentage points. Five distinct lines, each with a unique color and marker shape, represent different configurations or methods: a blue line with circle markers starts at ~95% AUC at N=0 and rises steadily to ~100% by N=20; an orange line with diamond markers begins at ~85% and increases to ~100%; a green line with star markers starts at ~87% and climbs to ~99%; a red line with square markers begins at ~88% and plateaus near 100%; and a purple line with triangle markers starts low at ~80%, jumps sharply to ~101% around N=7, then declines to ~94% by N=20. All lines generally trend upward with increasing N, though the purple line exhibits a distinct peak and subsequent drop, suggesting a non-monotonic relationship for that method.
